```python
def add_string(lst, fmt):
    return [fmt.format(x) for x in lst]
```

This formats each element into the `{0}` placeholder, so `add_string([1,2,3,4],'temp{0}')` returns `['temp1', 'temp2', 'temp3', 'temp4']`. The team note's other option, `string + str(i)`, would produce `'temp{0}1'`, so I didn't use it.
